units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Welcome to the story of Luxembourg.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And I'm Ben. Over the next hour or so, we're going to tell the story of one of the strangest and most successful countries in Europe: the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: It's small. You could drive across it in about an hour, and its population is smaller than that of many a single city.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And yet it's been fought over by emperors and kings for more than a thousand years.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's been a fortress, a province, a battlefield, a steel empire, a banking center, and one of the founding members of the European Union.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And it's the last grand duchy in the world.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: So how did a tiny territory on the edge of the great powers end up with all of that history?

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I suspect the answer is rock, iron, borders, and stubbornness.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. It's the story of a people who, in the words of their own national motto, want to remain what they are.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: We'll move in order, from the Stone Age to the present day.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: So settle in, and let's begin with a swap of land beside a river.
